evidence: Grounded as an acknowledged contract gap, narrowed to truthful source-unavailable handling rather than a requirement to archive transcripts. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:241,251,255-259 specify asynchronous processing, durable pending requests, explicit completion, transcript identity/processed-through coverage and summary path; they leave lifecycle/retry/result details open. Full-text searches for transcript, source, input, unavailable, unreadable, retention, snapshot, failure, result, coverage and equivalents across all four artifacts find no rule that preserves source readability, detects changed/truncated source, or records terminal incomplete/unavailable processing. HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:37 acknowledges transcripts can be unavailable for native-session resume, but its fresh-session recovery fallback does not dispose of a pending summary request. DESIGN-NOTES.md:151,170-174 and HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:96 address structural/reconciliation failures, not this later transcript contract; DESIGN-NOTES.md:183-189 explicitly bounds that older operation machinery. If a durable request is retried after its source is unavailable, persistence of the request cannot yield covered output; leaving it pending or marking completion without coverage conflicts with explicit completion/coverage and the vision's visible repairable progress (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:92-94). No actual transcript loss or harness-retention behavior is asserted.
